title: How Nigeria voted
lede: Who won each state in Nigeria's presidential elections, from the votes declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

elections.headline: The first time a sitting president lost
elections.text: Muhammadu Buhari of the new APC beat President Goodluck Jonathan of the PDP, which had won every presidential election since military rule ended in 1999. Jonathan conceded before the result was declared.

elections.headline: Buhari re-elected, the map splits
elections.text: Buhari won a second term against Atiku Abubakar. The APC took most of the north and four of the six south-western states; the PDP took every state in the south-east and south-south, and much of the middle belt.

elections.headline: Four strong candidates, three regions
elections.text: Bola Tinubu won with the smallest share of these three elections. Peter Obi of the Labour Party won the south-east, the FCT and Tinubu's home state of Lagos; Rabiu Kwankwaso won Kano. The Supreme Court upheld the result on 26 October 2023.

corrections.note: The compiled table gives 196,567, but its own share (52.47%) and Yobe's total of valid votes (378,397) both need 198,567, the figure other reports of the declaration give.

known_gaps.text: The 37 state results here, as announced at INEC's national collation centre and reported in the press, do not add up exactly to the national totals INEC declared: they give Tinubu 10,694 more votes, Obi 10,516 fewer and Atiku 2,230 fewer (all under 0.2% of a candidate's votes). Kwara's own figures are also 40 votes more than its total of valid votes. The national figures on this page are INEC's declared totals and the state figures are as announced. Checking each state against INEC's own result sheets (Form EC8D) is still to do.

rule: To win in the first round, the winner needs the most votes and at least a quarter of the votes in two-thirds of the 36 states and the FCT (Constitution of Nigeria 1999, section 134(2)). Two-thirds of 36 states is 24.
